tests.description: The muzzle, the breech, the antenna top, aiming and firing of a 3D tank made of nested custom objects follow every transformation (ToParentX/Y/Z, FromParentX/Y/Z), compared with what the renderer draws.
tests.name: TankConversions3D
source: // Gameplay test: a 3D tank (a custom object) containing a turret (a custom
// object) containing a cannon and an antenna (3D boxes). The scene only uses
// the interface of the tank: Tank3D.MuzzleX/Y/Z(), BreechX/Y/Z(),
// AntennaTopX/Y/Z() (converted with ToParentX/Y/Z at each level) and
// AimAt(x, y, z) (converted with FromParentX/Y/Z at each level). Everything is
// compared with where the renderer (THREE) actually draws the parts.
const random = (min, max) => min + Math.random() * (max - min);
/** Where THREE draws a point of a box (in its unit box, -0.5 to 0.5), in the scene. */
const pointOf = (state, name) => new THREE.Vector3(state[name + 'X'], state[name + 'Y'], state[name + 'Z']);
new THREE.Vector3(box.getX() + box.getWidth() / 2, box.getY() + box.getHeight() / 2, box.getZ() + box.getDepth() / 2);
/** Any transformation of the tank, and anything inside it. */
// 1. Whatever the transformations (tilted, flipped, scaled differently on
// each axis), the events give the muzzle, the breech and the top of the
// antenna that the game draws - and the flag attached by the scene sits on it.
const worst = { muzzle: 0, breech: 0, antennaTop: 0, attachedFlag: 0 };
report('Muzzle, breech and antenna top, 200 random frames x 4 tanks', worst, 1e-3);
await harness.takeScreenshot('Random transformations - flags on the antennas', { fullResolution: true });
// 2. Shells fired by the scene from Tank3D.MuzzleX/Y/Z, along the direction
// from Breech to Muzzle, fly along the drawn barrel - pitch and tilt included.
// 300 pixels per second, for 30 or 31 frames.
harness.assert(isEveryShellInFront, 'Every shell flew forward from the muzzle, at its speed');
await harness.takeScreenshot('Shells fired from the muzzles along the barrels', { fullResolution: true });
// 3. AimAt(x, y, z): the tank turns its turret toward the target seen in its
// own space (FromParentX/Y), and the turret raises its cannon toward it seen
// in its space (FromParentX/Z): every drawn barrel passes through the target.
const target = new THREE.Vector3(random(0, 800), random(0, 600), random(-40, 120));
report(`Aim at a point (FromParentX/Y/Z), ${checkedCount} aims`, { targetToBarrelLineDistance: worstDistance }, 1e-3);
harness.assert(isEveryTargetInFront, 'Every barrel points toward its target, not away from it');
await harness.takeScreenshot('Aiming at the floating target (FromParentX-Y-Z) and firing', { fullResolution: true });
await harness.takeScreenshot('Aiming at a target on the ground after the tanks moved', { fullResolution: true });
// 4. A collapsed tank (a scale of 0 on an axis) still answers numbers.
'Aiming a collapsed tank never gives a NaN rotation'
